eyebrow: Python for Data Science · Chapter 1, Lesson 3
subtitle: Store a value, know its type, decide and repeat — the core of the language.

code:
customer = "Ada"
orders = 12
avg_order = 48.5
is_active = True

print(type(customer), type(orders),
      type(avg_order), type(is_active))
# <class 'str'> <class 'int'> <class 'float'> <class 'bool'>
caption: Python decides the type from the value — no DECLARE, no type stated up front.

code:
total = orders * avg_order        # 582.0
print(7 / 2, 7 // 2, 7 % 2)        # 3.5 3 1

print(f"{customer} spent {total:.2f} across {orders} orders")
# Ada spent 582.00 across 12 orders
caption: / always gives a float, // floor-divides, % gives the remainder; :.2f formats money.

code:
value = None
print(value is None)        # True  (not == None)

print(bool(0), bool(""), bool([]))   # False False False
print(bool("a"))                      # True
caption: None means "no value", like NULL in SQL. 0, "", and [] are all falsy.
Indentation (4 spaces) defines the block — Python's cousin of a T-SQL CASE WHEN.

code:
totals = [20.0, 55.5, 130.0]
running = 0
for t in totals:
    running += t
    print(t, running)
# 20.0 20.0 / 55.5 75.5 / 130.0 205.5
caption: enumerate() adds the index; range(3) gives 0,1,2; break exits, continue skips ahead.
Never compare floats with ==; and + on strings concatenates — the classic numbers-read-as-text bug.
